scope: Static implementation review and disposable local TLS fixtures; no live runtime data.

transport.library: urllib3==2.8.0 (already included in the audited runtime closure, now explicitly pinned)
transport.lifecycle: One verified SSLContext and pool manager per process; PID guard recreates after fork; four origin pools maximum
transport.deadline_handling: Pool waiting consumes the existing 12-second budget; remaining connect/read time and per-chunk response checks do not increase the timeout
transport.tls_certificate_verification: CERT_REQUIRED with system trust and hostname verification
transport.signed_requests: Fresh timestamp, nonce and exact-body v1/v2 HMAC on each caller attempt; no auth, cookies or player state stored in the pool
transport.request_limit_reason: Matches the existing Core JSON request limit
transport.response_handling: Drained valid-size responses are reused; oversized, partial and failing streams are closed/discarded and pool permits are released
transport.metrics: Only aggregate requests, failures, in-flight count, peak count, queue wait and HTTP duration sums/maxima; no origins, keys, IDs or payloads

ci_correction: Legacy backup-only workflow now installs runtime requirements and pytest and executes the streaming tests; contents permission is read-only and checkout does not persist credentials.
limitations: Local TLS fixtures demonstrate transport behavior, not live 500/1000-session latency or soak completion.
AnyIO worker count remains unchanged. The existing project latency threshold and network timeout were not relaxed.
No sandbox/production staged source pins or Railway settings were changed.
